extracted.intended_audience: MathML authors and renderer implementers (web developers, browser/vendor engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Specification of MathML presentation elements, token types, and attributes governing visual rendering, linebreaking, and spacing; intended to guide authors of MathML and implementers of MathML renderers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linebreaking attributes (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes that determine the desirability of a linebreak at a specific operator or space (whether a break is required or inhibited). These attributes can only be set on mo and mspace elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls when breaks are allowed/forbidden/suggested (see specific attributes under mo). Use these attributes on mo/mspace to encode linebreaking policy. See 3.2.5.2.2 for details and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator display/position on linebreak
rubrics_metrics.description: When a linebreak occurs, attributes determine whether the operator will appear at the end of the line, at the beginning of the next line, or in both positions, and how much vertical space should be added after the linebreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes may be set on mo elements or inherited from mstyle/math. Use linebreakstyle, lineleading, and related attributes to control appearance; see examples of forced linebreaks/indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation after linebreak
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes that determine the indentation of the line following a linebreak, including indenting so that the next line aligns with some point in a previous line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set on mo elements or inherited from mstyle or math. Use indentalign, indentalignlast, indenttarget, etc., to control alignment of continued lines (see example where indenttarget references an operator id).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced linebreaks and forced alignment (example guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example demonstrating forced linebreaks, linebreakstyle, and forced alignment using indentalign/indenttarget, with notes on defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that indentalignlast defaults to indentalign, and explicit linebreakstyle='before' is unnecessary because 'before' is the default. Use id attributes to target indentation alignment points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token elements (list and intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Token elements represent smallest units of mathematical notation: mi (identifier), mn (number), mo (operator/fence/separator/accent), mtext (text), mspace (space), ms (string literal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Token elements are roughly analogous to words in text and carry meaning. mglyph may be used within token elements for non-standard symbols. Token content rules and attributes are specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: mglyph for non-standard symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: mglyph may be used within token elements to represent non-standard symbols as images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Web contexts prefer using HTML img. mglyph is not in MathML-Core. A JavaScript polyfill can implement mglyph using img. The src attribute uniquely identifies an mglyph; alt is required and should be descriptive for audio renderers or fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: General layout schemata
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation layout elements and their roles: mrow, mfrac, msqrt, mroot, mstyle, merror, mpadded, mphantom, mfenced, menclose (and their semantics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate layout element for the intended visual structure (fractions, radicals, fenced expressions, style changes, error messages, padding/phantom content, enclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and limit schemata
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements for scripts and limits: msub, msup, msubsup, munder, mover, munderover, mmultiscripts (attach subscripts/superscripts/underscripts/overscripts or multiple scripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elements to represent sub/superscripts and limit-like constructs. Behavior with displaystyle/scriptlevel is described in 3.1.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and matrices elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements for tabular/math-matrix layouts: mtable, mtr, mtd, maligngroup, malignmark (alignment markers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elements to represent matrices/tables; use maligngroup/malignmark for alignment control within columns/rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary math layout elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements for elementary math layouts such as mstack, mlongdiv, msgroup, msrow, mscarries, mscarry, msline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these for aligned columns, long division visuals, carry/borrow rows, and horizontal lines inside stacked layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlivening expressions (actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: maction binds actions to a sub-expression to enliven expressions (e.g., interactive behaviors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use maction when interaction or dynamic behavior is required on sub-expressions; consider rendering and accessibility implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes common to presentation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation elements accept global attributes plus MathML-specific core attributes; in MathML 3 they were restricted to mstyle but in this spec they are allowed on any presentation element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes listed in 2.1.6 and MathML-Core global attributes apply. Many visual attributes are intended for presentation only and should not affect semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Core Attributes (mathcolor, mathbackground, scriptlevel, displaystyle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual attributes intended primarily for rendering: mathcolor (foreground color, inherited), mathbackground (background color/transparent), scriptlevel (change displaystyle for children), displaystyle (change displaystyle for children).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons are ASCII case-insensitive. Renderers should inherit foreground color from surrounding context. mathbackground default is transparent; exact extent of background region is not precisely defined by spec.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Full-only Attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional presentation attributes supported in MathML Full: scriptsizemultiplier, scriptminsize, infixlinebreakstyle, decimalcharacter, with specified defaults and meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: scriptsizemultiplier controls font-size multiplier for scriptlevel; scriptminsize sets minimum font size; infixlinebreakstyle sets default linebreakstyle for infix operators; decimalcharacter indicates decimal alignment character for mstack. Use according to section 3.1.9.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of processing for script-related attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: When scriptlevel is changed incrementally by an element that also sets other attributes, attributes should be processed in this specific order: scriptsizemultiplier, scriptminsize, scriptlevel, mathsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this processing order to ensure predictable combined effects of script-related attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreground color inheritance guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML renderer should inherit the foreground color used in the context in which the MathML appears (since MathML expressions are often embedded in textual formats like HTML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML does not specify the mechanism of inheritance from the rendering environment; renderers should attempt to use contextual foreground color for compatibility with surrounding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathbackground extent and overlap undefined
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec does not define precise extent of region affected by mathbackground when negative spacing or overlapping drawings occur; it should lie behind all drawing of the content and not behind surrounding expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renderers should ensure background lies behind content drawing and not behind surrounding expressions; behavior with negative spacing overlaps is unspecified by these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token element content and rendering rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Character data is only allowed as content of token elements; whitespace between elements is ignored. Token elements (other than mspace) should be rendered as their content (glyphs/images) with mathematics style attributes applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mspace is rendered as blank space; renderers should respect directional characteristics and spacing rules specific to token types. mglyph may appear as image children of token elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: mglyph attributes and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: mglyph displays an image to represent a non-standard symbol; attributes include required src and alt, optional width/height, valign, and mathbackground applies but mathcolor has no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one of width/height provided, scale to preserve aspect ratio; if none given, use natural image size. alt should be descriptive for fallbacks and audio renderers. mglyph not in MathML-Core; prefer HTML img in web contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathvariant, mathsize, and dir on token elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Token elements accept mathematics style attributes: mathvariant (logical class such as italic, bold, sans-serif, etc.), mathsize (small|normal|big|length), and dir (ltr|rtl) with specified defaults and semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mathvariant conveys semantic/typographic class (not merely styling). Renderers should map mathvariant to appropriate fonts where possible, avoid misleading mappings (e.g., do not render sans-serif tokens in Times). Some defaults are special (mi single-character content defaults to italic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and equivalence with Unicode mathematical alphanumeric symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain mathvariant+character combinations correspond to Unicode mathematical alphanumeric symbols; those combinations should be supported by renderers and visually distinguished when fonts allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renderers should support combinations corresponding to Unicode characters and may ignore/support others; authors should recognize that support for non-Unicode combinations may vary across renderers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding HTML/SVG or other formats in MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML can combine with other formats by allowing additional elements as children of mtext or other leaf elements; directionality, font size, and other font attributes should inherit from containing leaf element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: embed other formats by extending schema to allow them in mtext. When embedding (example: SVG inside mtext), ensure rendering attributes match expected leaf-element typography and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: mi (identifier) element semantics and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: mi represents a symbolic name or arbitrary text rendered as an identifier (variables, function names, symbolic constants). It is a presentation element and indicates rendering as an identifier rather than guaranteed semantic identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use mi for subscripted or primed variables (use msub/msup). Arbitrary terms or placeholders can use mi; if semantics require guaranteed identifier, use content markup ci. mi elements accept mathvariant defaulting behavior (single-character mi default italic).

rubrics_metrics.name: mn (number) element semantics and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: mn represents a numeric literal (sequence of digits, decimal point, etc.) intended to render as a numeric literal; typically rendered unslanted with no extra spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mn should be reserved for content intended to represent numeric quantities. Do not represent complex numbers, negative numbers, fractions (ratios), or named numeric constants using mn alone; use composite presentation elements for those cases (examples provided). mn accepts mathematics style attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: mo (operator/fence/separator/accent) element general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: mo represents operators and things rendered as operators (infix/prefix/postfix, fences, separators, accents). mo default attribute values are often set from an operator dictionary; renderers should attempt to render content literally where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mo elements control spacing, stretching, symmetry, accent behavior, and linebreaking. Default values can come from mstyle, math, document, or the operator dictionary; where fonts are incomplete, renderers may approximate characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: mo dictionary-based attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes whose defaults are dictionary-based: form (prefix|infix|postfix), lspace, rspace, stretchy, symmetric, maxsize, minsize, largeop, movablelimits, accent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: form is set by operator position and affects dictionary lookup. lspace/rspace control spacing around operators (default thickmathspace). stretchy/symmetric control stretching behavior and symmetry around math axis. maxsize/minsize limit stretchy operator size (unitless or percentage multiples). largeop and movablelimits control behavior under displaystyle and limit movement. accent indicates accent behavior for underscripts/overscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: mo linebreaking attributes (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linebreaking-related mo attributes: linebreak (auto|newline|nobreak|goodbreak|badbreak), lineleading (amount of vertical space after a linebreak), linebreakstyle (before|after|duplicate|infixlinebreakstyle), infixlinebreakstyle (use mstyle/app-specified infix default), linebreakmultchar (character to make InvisibleTimes visible at a break).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: linebreak values indicate desirability of breaking at this operator; newline forces a break, nobreak forbids, goodbreak/badbreak suggest quality. linebreakstyle controls where operator appears on break (before/after/duplicate). lineleading can be used to adjust leading after breaks (default 100%). linebreakmultchar sets visible character for InvisibleTimes at linebreaks. Note: linebreak values on adjacent mo and mspace do not interact; linebreak='nobreak' on an mo prevents breaks on either side of that mo but does not block breaks on neighboring (possibly nested) mo/mspace by itself.
